The slot fits a phone 75 mm wide with a lip of at least 8 mm
A watertight STL is saved

lessons.title: Find your way around FreeCAD
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner FreeCAD. Make a new document, switch to the Part Design workbench, create a body and move the view.

lessons.title: Your first sketch
lessons.goal: Teach FreeCAD sketching by drawing a closed rectangle on the XY plane of a Part Design body.

lessons.title: Constrain it fully
lessons.goal: Teach FreeCAD sketch constraints. Add length, width and position until the rectangle is fully constrained at 60 by 40 mm.

lessons.title: Pad it into a plate
lessons.goal: Teach the Pad tool in FreeCAD Part Design by turning the 60 by 40 mm sketch into a plate 5 mm thick.

lessons.title: Sketch on a face and cut holes
lessons.goal: Teach sketching on a face and the Pocket tool in FreeCAD by cutting two 4 mm screw holes through the plate.

lessons.title: Add the hook
lessons.goal: Teach adding a second feature in FreeCAD by sketching on the face of the plate and padding a hook 30 mm out.

lessons.title: Fillets and chamfers
lessons.goal: Teach the Fillet and Chamfer tools in FreeCAD by rounding the outer edges of the hook by 2 mm.

lessons.title: Mirror and pattern
lessons.goal: Teach the Mirror and Linear Pattern tools in FreeCAD by repeating the screw hole four times along the plate.

lessons.title: Change a dimension
lessons.goal: Teach parametric editing in FreeCAD. Reopen the first sketch, change 60 mm to 80 mm and fix what breaks.

lessons.title: Export an STL to print
lessons.goal: Teach exporting a FreeCAD body as an STL for 3D printing and checking the size before you print.

project.title: A WordPress blog in one Compose file
checks: docker compose ps shows two running services
Both services store their data in named volumes
localhost port 8080 answers with the WordPress setup page

lessons.title: Run your first container
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Docker Desktop on a Mac. Run docker run hello-world in the terminal, then read docker ps -a and docker images to see the container and the image it came from.

lessons.title: Serve a page and map a port
lessons.goal: Teach detached containers and port mapping in Docker by running nginx with -d, --name web and -p 8080:80, then opening localhost:8080 in the browser to see its welcome page.

lessons.title: Logs, exec, stop and remove
lessons.goal: Teach looking after a Docker container. Read docker logs web, open a shell inside it with docker exec -it web sh, then stop and remove it with docker stop and docker rm.

lessons.title: Write a Dockerfile
lessons.goal: Teach the Dockerfile instructions FROM and COPY by making a site folder with your own index.html and a Dockerfile that copies it into an nginx:alpine image.

lessons.title: Build and tag your image
lessons.goal: Teach docker build, tags and the layer cache by building the site as my-site:1.0, running it on port 8080, changing the page and building my-site:1.1.

lessons.title: Edit live with a bind mount
lessons.goal: Teach Docker bind mounts by running nginx with -v so the site folder on the Mac is the folder it serves, then editing index.html and seeing the change with no rebuild.

lessons.title: Keep data in a named volume
lessons.goal: Teach Docker named volumes by adding a line to log.txt in a volume named notes from one alpine container, then from a second, and reading both lines back from a third.

lessons.title: One file to run it with Compose
lessons.goal: Teach Docker Compose by writing compose.yaml with one web service that builds the site image, maps port 8080 and mounts the site folder, then using docker compose up -d and down.

lessons.title: Add a database service
lessons.goal: Teach Compose services, environment values and the shared network by adding a Postgres service named db with a password and a named volume, then reaching db by name from web.

project.title: A bake sale sales report
checks: Each sale row gets its price from an XLOOKUP on a price list
A SUMIF or a PivotTable totals sales for each item
A chart of sales by item has a title

lessons.title: Enter a budget in cells and ranges
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Excel on a Mac. Type a month of spending into a new workbook with headers for item, category, planned and actual in row 1 and twelve rows below, then save budget.xlsx.

lessons.title: Write your first formulas
lessons.goal: Teach Excel formulas with the equals sign, cell references and the + - * / operators by working out planned minus actual for the first budget item in E2.

lessons.title: Totals with SUM, AVERAGE and MAX
lessons.goal: Teach Excel functions and ranges with SUM, AVERAGE, MIN and MAX by adding a totals row under the budget and finding the average and the largest amount spent.

lessons.title: Relative and absolute references
lessons.goal: Teach relative and absolute references in Excel. Fill the difference formula down to row 13, then lock the total with $D$14 to work out each item's share of spending.

lessons.title: SUMIF and COUNTIF
lessons.goal: Teach SUMIF and COUNTIF in Excel by building a summary beside the budget that totals the spending and counts the items in each category.

lessons.title: Look things up with XLOOKUP
lessons.goal: Teach XLOOKUP in Excel by pulling each category's monthly limit from a small limits table into the budget rows, with a message for a category that is not found.

lessons.title: Sort and filter
lessons.goal: Teach Sort and Filter in Excel by sorting the budget from the largest amount to the smallest, then filtering it to show only the Food category.

lessons.title: Summarise with a PivotTable
lessons.goal: Teach PivotTables in Excel by summarising the budget on a new sheet, with Category in the rows and the sum of Actual in the values.

lessons.title: Make a chart
lessons.goal: Teach Excel charts by turning the category summary into a column chart with a chart title and axis titles, placed beside the budget.

project.title: A two-screen sign-in flow
checks: Two phone frames are built with auto layout
A button component set with two variants is used on both frames
A prototype link joins the frames and two PNG files are saved

lessons.title: Make a file and your first frame
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Figma. Make a design file named Weather, add a frame with the Frame tool from a phone preset, rename it Home, and practice zooming and panning the canvas.

lessons.title: Shapes, text and fills
lessons.goal: Teach Figma shapes and text by drawing a rounded card on Home with the Rectangle tool, a yellow sun with the Ellipse tool and the temperature in large type with the Text tool.

lessons.title: Name, group and align layers
lessons.goal: Teach the Figma Layers panel and the align tools by naming every layer of the weather card, grouping the sun with the temperature and centering the group on the card.

lessons.title: Auto layout for the today card
lessons.goal: Teach Figma auto layout (Shift+A) by turning the weather card into a vertical auto layout frame with 16 padding and 8 between items, then adding a line of text and watching the card grow.

lessons.title: Color and text styles
lessons.goal: Teach Figma styles by saving two color styles and two text styles from the weather card, applying them to its layers, then changing one style and watching every layer that uses it update.

lessons.title: Make a component for the day chip
lessons.goal: Teach Figma components by building a small day chip with a day name and a temperature, making it a component and placing five instances in a row on Home, each with its own text.

lessons.title: Add a selected variant
lessons.goal: Teach Figma variants by adding a second variant to Day chip, naming the property State with the values Default and Selected, and switching one instance on Home to Selected.

lessons.title: Link two frames in a prototype
lessons.goal: Teach Figma prototyping by adding a second frame named Details, linking a Day chip to it with an On tap, Navigate to interaction, adding a way back and playing the prototype.

lessons.title: Export the screens
lessons.goal: Teach exporting from Figma by adding export settings to the Home and Details frames, PNG at 2x, and saving both files to the Mac.

project.title: A cable clip for a desk edge
checks: One solid body and every sketch fully constrained
The clip opening is 20 mm and the cable hole is 5 mm across
An STL of the clip is saved

lessons.title: Find your way around Fusion
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Autodesk Fusion. Start a new design, save it as Box, set the units to millimeters, and tour the Browser, the Timeline and the ViewCube while orbiting the view.

lessons.title: Sketch the outline of the box
lessons.goal: Teach starting a sketch in Fusion by choosing Create Sketch on the XY plane, drawing a Center Rectangle from the origin for the footprint of a box and finishing the sketch.

lessons.title: Dimension and constrain the sketch
lessons.goal: Teach Fusion sketch dimensions and constraints by sizing the box rectangle to 80 by 50 mm with Sketch Dimension and checking that every line turns black, fully constrained.

lessons.title: Extrude it into a block
lessons.goal: Teach the Extrude tool in Fusion by pulling the 80 by 50 mm profile up 30 mm into a solid block and finding the new feature in the Timeline.

lessons.title: Round the corners with Fillet
lessons.goal: Teach the Fillet tool in Fusion by rounding the four upright edges of the block with a 6 mm radius, and how Fillet differs from Chamfer.

lessons.title: Hollow it out with Shell
lessons.goal: Teach the Shell tool in Fusion by removing the top face of the block and leaving walls and a floor 2 mm thick, which turns the block into an open box.

lessons.title: Add a cable hole
lessons.goal: Teach the Hole tool in Fusion by placing an 8 mm hole through one short wall of the box, centered on that wall, for a charging cable.

lessons.title: Make a lid as a second component
lessons.goal: Teach Fusion components by turning the box body into a component named Base, then making a new component named Lid and extruding a 3 mm lid from the projected outline of the box.

lessons.title: Change a size from the Timeline
lessons.goal: Teach parametric editing in Fusion. Reopen the first sketch from the Timeline, change 80 mm to 100 mm and check that the fillets, the shell, the hole and the lid all rebuild.

lessons.title: Export both parts as STL
lessons.goal: Teach exporting from Fusion for 3D printing by saving the Base and the Lid of the box as two STL mesh files and checking their size before printing.

project.title: A film list with a merged pull request
checks: The GitHub repository has at least four commits on main
One merged pull request came from a separate branch
A .gitignore is committed and git status reports a clean working tree

lessons.title: Set up Git and make a repository
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Git in the macOS Terminal. Set user.name and user.email with git config, make a cookbook folder, run git init -b main inside it and read git status.

lessons.title: Stage and commit
lessons.goal: Teach the Git working tree, the staging area and commits by writing pancakes.md in the cookbook, staging it with git add and saving it with git commit -m.

lessons.title: See what changed with log and diff
lessons.goal: Teach git diff, git diff --staged and git log --oneline by changing the pancake recipe in the cookbook twice and committing each change with a clear message.

lessons.title: Undo a change and ignore files
lessons.goal: Teach git restore, git restore --staged and .gitignore by throwing away a bad edit to pancakes.md, unstaging a file and keeping .DS_Store out of the cookbook for good.

lessons.title: Work on a branch
lessons.goal: Teach Git branches with git switch -c and git branch by adding waffles.md to the cookbook on a branch named add-waffles while main stays as it was.

lessons.title: Merge a branch
lessons.goal: Teach git merge and reading git log --oneline --graph by merging add-waffles into main in the cookbook and deleting the branch once it is merged.

lessons.title: Fix a merge conflict
lessons.goal: Teach resolving a Git merge conflict. Change the same line of pancakes.md on main and on a branch, merge, read the conflict markers, choose the final text and commit the merge.

lessons.title: Connect to GitHub with an SSH key
lessons.goal: Teach connecting Git on a Mac to GitHub. Make an ed25519 key with ssh-keygen, add the public key to the GitHub account and test the link with ssh -T git@github.com.

lessons.title: Push the cookbook to GitHub
lessons.goal: Teach Git remotes by making an empty repository on GitHub, linking it with git remote add origin and sending the cookbook up with git push -u origin main.

lessons.title: Open a pull request
lessons.goal: Teach the GitHub pull request flow. Push a branch that adds syrup.md to the cookbook, open a pull request on github.com, read the diff, merge it and update main with git pull.

project.title: A key and door room
checks: The player is a CharacterBody2D whose script calls move_and_slide
A signal from an Area2D key frees a StaticBody2D door
A Label changes when the player reaches the exit

lessons.title: Make a project and a first scene
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Godot 4. Make a new project, tour the Scene, FileSystem and Inspector docks, add a Node2D root named Main, save it as main.tscn and set it as the main scene.

lessons.title: Nodes and the scene tree
lessons.goal: Teach Godot nodes and parent and child trees by adding a Sprite2D under Main that shows icon.svg, moving it to 200, 150 in the Inspector and running the project.

lessons.title: Your first GDScript
lessons.goal: Teach GDScript in Godot 4 by attaching a script to the Sprite2D that prints a line in _ready and spins the sprite in _process using delta and an exported speed variable.

lessons.title: A player that moves
lessons.goal: Teach player movement in Godot 4. Build player.tscn from a CharacterBody2D, a Sprite2D and a CollisionShape2D, then read Input.get_vector, set velocity and call move_and_slide.

lessons.title: Put the player in a walled room
lessons.goal: Teach instancing scenes and static collisions in Godot 4 by adding player.tscn to Main and boxing it in with four StaticBody2D walls that each have a CollisionShape2D.

lessons.title: A coin and the body_entered signal
lessons.goal: Teach Godot signals by building coin.tscn from an Area2D, connecting its body_entered signal to its own script and calling queue_free when the player touches the coin.

lessons.title: Count coins with your own signal
lessons.goal: Teach custom signals in GDScript by declaring a collected signal in the coin, emitting it on pickup and connecting five coin instances to one function in Main that adds to a score.

lessons.title: Show the score in a Label
lessons.goal: Teach Godot UI nodes by adding a CanvasLayer with a Label to Main and setting its text to the word Coins and the score each time a coin is collected.

lessons.title: A countdown with a Timer node
lessons.goal: Teach the Godot Timer node and its timeout signal by giving the coin game a 30 second countdown, shown in a second Label, that stops the game when it reaches zero.

lessons.title: Export the game for Mac
lessons.goal: Teach exporting from Godot 4. Download the export templates, add a macOS preset in the Export window, set a bundle identifier and export the coin game as an app you can open.

project.title: A fundraiser tracker
checks: At least twelve donation rows with a SUMIF total for each team
A VLOOKUP or INDEX and MATCH pulls each team's goal
A chart compares money raised with the goal for each team

lessons.title: Start a sign-up sheet
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Google Sheets. Make a new spreadsheet named Club sign-ups, add headers for name, grade, event and paid, enter ten rows and freeze the header row.

lessons.title: Formulas and cell references
lessons.goal: Teach Google Sheets formulas with the equals sign, cell references, SUM and COUNTA by counting the sign-ups, totalling the money paid and working out the spots left from a cap of 30.

lessons.title: Relative and absolute references
lessons.goal: Teach relative and absolute references in Google Sheets by filling a formula down that takes each member's payment away from a club fee kept in one cell locked with $ signs.

lessons.title: COUNTIF and SUMIF
lessons.goal: Teach COUNTIF and SUMIF in Google Sheets by building a summary that counts the sign-ups and totals the money paid for each event.

lessons.title: Look up a fee with VLOOKUP
lessons.goal: Teach VLOOKUP with an exact match in Google Sheets by pulling each event's fee from an Events tab into the sign-up rows in place of the single club fee.

lessons.title: INDEX and MATCH
lessons.goal: Teach INDEX and MATCH in Google Sheets by finding which event meets in a given room on the Events tab, a lookup to the left that VLOOKUP cannot do.

lessons.title: Sort and filter
lessons.goal: Teach sorting and filtering in Google Sheets. Sort the sign-ups by event and then by name, then create a filter that shows only the members who still owe money.

lessons.title: Count with a pivot table
lessons.goal: Teach pivot tables in Google Sheets by making one on a new tab with Event in the rows, Grade in the columns and a count of names in the values.

lessons.title: Chart the sign-ups
lessons.goal: Teach charts in Google Sheets by turning the event summary into a bar chart with a chart title and axis titles.

project.title: A notebook report on your own numbers
checks: After Restart Kernel and Run All Cells no cell shows an error
It has at least two Markdown cells and one chart image in an output
An HTML export is saved next to the notebook

lessons.title: Start Jupyter and run a cell
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Jupyter. Start JupyterLab from the terminal with jupyter lab, make a notebook named steps.ipynb and run one Python cell with Shift+Return.

lessons.title: Command mode and edit mode
lessons.goal: Teach the two Jupyter notebook modes and the keys A, B, D D, M and Y by adding cells to steps.ipynb that hold a week of step counts in a list and print the total.

lessons.title: Run order and what the kernel keeps
lessons.goal: Teach how a Jupyter kernel keeps variables between cells and why run order matters, by changing a daily goal in one cell of steps.ipynb and rerunning the cell that compares the steps to it.

lessons.title: Write notes in Markdown cells
lessons.goal: Teach Jupyter Markdown cells by giving steps.ipynb a title, a heading for each part, a bullet list that says what the numbers mean and one phrase in bold.

lessons.title: Help, tab completion and magics
lessons.goal: Teach finding help inside Jupyter with Tab, Shift+Tab and a question mark, and the %timeit and %whos magics, by timing two ways to total the week of steps.

lessons.title: Install a package and draw a chart
lessons.goal: Teach installing a package from a Jupyter cell with %pip install matplotlib, then drawing a bar chart of steps per day that shows under the cell, with a title and axis labels.

lessons.title: Restart and run all
lessons.goal: Teach the Jupyter Kernel menu. Use Restart Kernel and Run All Cells on steps.ipynb, find the cell that fails because it leans on a cell that was deleted, and fix the order.

lessons.title: Export and share the notebook
lessons.goal: Teach sharing a Jupyter notebook. Rerun steps.ipynb from the top so it is clean, then use Save and Export Notebook As in the File menu to save an HTML copy anyone can open.

project.title: A hinge that opens and closes
checks: The Part Studio has two parts and every sketch is fully defined
A Revolute mate joins the two leaves in an assembly
An STL of one leaf is exported

lessons.title: Make a document and look around
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Onshape. Create a document named Wheel stand, set the units to millimeters, find the Part Studio and Assembly tabs and the Feature list, and rename the Part Studio to Parts.

lessons.title: Sketch the bracket outline
lessons.goal: Teach sketching in an Onshape Part Studio by starting a sketch on the Front plane and drawing the U-shaped outline of a bracket with the Line tool, ending where it began.

lessons.title: Dimension and constrain the sketch
lessons.goal: Teach Onshape dimensions and constraints by making the bracket outline 40 mm wide and 50 mm tall with 5 mm walls, using Equal and Symmetric until the sketch turns black.

lessons.title: Extrude the bracket
lessons.goal: Teach the Extrude tool in Onshape by turning the U-shaped sketch into a solid 20 mm deep and renaming the new part to Bracket in the parts list.

lessons.title: Cut the axle holes
lessons.goal: Teach sketching on a face and Extrude with Remove in Onshape by drawing a 6 mm circle 35 mm up one arm of the Bracket and cutting it through both arms.

lessons.title: Round the edges with Fillet
lessons.goal: Teach the Fillet tool in Onshape by rounding the outer corners of the Bracket with a 3 mm radius and finding the new feature in the Feature list.

lessons.title: Add the wheel as a second part
lessons.goal: Teach making a second part in one Onshape Part Studio by sketching a 40 mm circle with a 6 mm hole and extruding it 20 mm as a new part named Wheel, centered between the arms.

lessons.title: Put the parts in an assembly
lessons.goal: Teach Onshape assemblies by inserting the Bracket and the Wheel into the Assembly tab and using Fix to hold the Bracket still.

lessons.title: Join them with a Revolute mate
lessons.goal: Teach Onshape mates and mate connectors by joining the hole in the Wheel to the hole in the Bracket with a Revolute mate, then dragging the Wheel to see it spin.

lessons.title: Save a version and export an STL
lessons.goal: Teach Onshape versions and export by saving a version named V1 of the Wheel stand document and exporting the Wheel as an STL file to the Mac.

project.title: A script that tidies a messy folder
checks: tidy.sh starts with a zsh shebang line and is executable
After a run no .txt, .jpg or .png file is left loose in the folder
It prints the number of files it moved

lessons.title: Find where you are
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner the macOS Terminal and zsh. Use pwd, ls and cd with tab completion to walk from the home folder to / and back, and show hidden files with ls -a.

lessons.title: Make folders and files
lessons.goal: Teach mkdir, mkdir -p and touch in the macOS Terminal by building a trail-log folder in the home folder with notes and photos folders inside and three empty day notes.

lessons.title: Copy, move, rename and delete
lessons.goal: Teach cp, mv, rm and rm -r in the macOS Terminal, and that rm has no undo, by copying day1.txt to day1-backup.txt, renaming day3.txt to summit.txt and removing a scratch folder.

lessons.title: Write lines into a file
lessons.goal: Teach echo with > and >> in the macOS Terminal, and how > overwrites while >> adds, by writing three lines about the weather and the trail into each of the three trail-log notes.

lessons.title: Read files with cat, less and head
lessons.goal: Teach reading text in the macOS Terminal with cat, less, head, tail and wc -l, and looking up a flag with man, by checking the three trail-log notes without opening an editor.

lessons.title: Match many files with wildcards
lessons.goal: Teach the * and ? wildcards in zsh by listing every .txt note in trail-log, copying day1.txt and day2.txt into a backup folder with one cp command and removing day1-backup.txt.

lessons.title: Pipes and grep
lessons.goal: Teach grep and the pipe in zsh by finding every line that mentions rain across the trail-log notes, sorting the matches, counting them with wc -l and saving the sorted lines to rain.txt.

lessons.title: Permissions and chmod
lessons.goal: Teach reading the rwx columns of ls -l and changing them with chmod in the macOS Terminal by making private.txt, a note that only its owner can read and write.

lessons.title: Write a shell script
lessons.goal: Teach a first zsh script on macOS. Write newday.sh in nano with a shebang line for zsh, make it executable with chmod +x and have it create a note named with today's date.

lessons.title: Variables, arguments and a loop
lessons.goal: Teach shell variables, the $1 argument and a for loop in zsh by writing count.sh, which takes a word and prints how many lines mention it in each trail-log note.

project.title: A marble maze with a finish line
checks: The Player has a Rigidbody and at least ten walls have colliders
A trigger at the goal changes a UI text when the Player enters it
A macOS build of the game is saved

lessons.title: Find your way around the editor
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner the Unity editor. Make a new 3D project, tour the Scene view, Game view, Hierarchy, Inspector and Project window, and save the scene as Main.

lessons.title: Build a floor and a player
lessons.goal: Teach Unity GameObjects and the Transform by adding a Plane named Floor at the origin and a Sphere named Player resting on it, placed by typing position values in the Inspector.

lessons.title: Components and materials
lessons.goal: Teach Unity components by adding a Rigidbody to the Player with Add Component, pressing Play to watch gravity act on it, and giving the Player and the Floor their own colored materials.

lessons.title: Write your first C# script
lessons.goal: Teach Unity C# scripts by making a PlayerController MonoBehaviour, attaching it to the Player and logging a line from Start and the position from Update to the Console.

lessons.title: Move the player with the keyboard
lessons.goal: Teach reading keyboard input in a Unity C# script and moving with physics by rolling the Player with AddForce on its Rigidbody in FixedUpdate, with a public speed field.

lessons.title: Walls and colliders
lessons.goal: Teach Unity colliders and how a Rigidbody reacts to them by boxing in the Floor with four Cube walls, so the rolling Player bounces back and cannot fall off the edge.

lessons.title: Make a coin prefab
lessons.goal: Teach Unity prefabs by shaping a flat Cylinder into a Coin with a script that spins it using Time.deltaTime, saving it as a prefab and placing eight copies on the Floor.

lessons.title: Collect coins with triggers
lessons.goal: Teach Unity trigger colliders and OnTriggerEnter by ticking Is Trigger on the Coin collider, tagging the prefab Coin and hiding each coin the Player touches.

lessons.title: Show the score on screen
lessons.goal: Teach Unity UI with a Canvas and a TextMeshPro text by counting collected coins in PlayerController and showing the count in the corner of the Game view.

lessons.title: Build the game for Mac
lessons.goal: Teach making a build in Unity. Add the Main scene to the scene list, choose the macOS platform, set the product name to Coin Roll and build an app that opens outside the editor.

project.title: A temperature converter, set up alone
checks: The folder holds temp.js, README.md and .vscode/settings.json
The workspace settings turn on editor.formatOnSave
node temp.js prints 212 for 100 degrees Celsius

lessons.title: Open a folder and make files
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner VS Code. Open a new folder named recipe-box, tour the Activity Bar and the Explorer, then make README.md and recipe.txt with six ingredient names, one per line.

lessons.title: The Command Palette and Quick Open
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code Command Palette (Shift+Cmd+P) and Quick Open (Cmd+P) by jumping between the two files and running Sort Lines Ascending on the ingredients in recipe.txt.

lessons.title: Edit many lines at once
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code multi-cursor editing with Option+click, Cmd+D and Option+Cmd+Down by turning the six plain lines into recipe.json, an array of objects that each have a name and cups.

lessons.title: Find and replace across files
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code find and replace in one file (Cmd+F) and across the whole folder (Shift+Cmd+F) by changing every cups to grams in recipe.json and README.md in one pass.

lessons.title: Run code in the integrated terminal
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code integrated terminal (Ctrl+`). Write scale.js that reads recipe.json and prints each amount doubled, run it with node, then split a second terminal beside the first.

lessons.title: Jump around and rename safely
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code code navigation. Move the doubling into a function in its own file, jump to it with Go to Definition (F12) and rename it to scaleRecipe everywhere with Rename Symbol (F2).

lessons.title: Install an extension
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code Extensions view (Shift+Cmd+X) by installing Prettier, choosing it as the default formatter and running Format Document on scale.js.

lessons.title: Settings and format on save
lessons.goal: Teach VS Code settings (Cmd+,) and how user and workspace settings differ by adding .vscode/settings.json to recipe-box with format on save turned on and a tab size of 2.

lessons.title: Find a bug with a breakpoint
lessons.goal: Teach the VS Code debugger. Set a breakpoint in scale.js, start it from Run and Debug with Node.js, step over lines and watch the variables to find why a new 250 gram item doubles to 250250.

project.title: A reading list app
checks: The project builds with no errors
A List inside a NavigationStack shows at least five rows
The detail view has a Button that changes a @State value

lessons.title: Make a new SwiftUI project
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner Xcode. Make a new iOS App project named Plants with the SwiftUI interface, then tour the navigator, the editor, the inspector and ContentView.swift.

lessons.title: See changes in the canvas preview
lessons.goal: Teach the Xcode canvas and the #Preview macro by changing the Hello, world text in ContentView to My plants and watching the preview update as you type.

lessons.title: Text, images and modifiers
lessons.goal: Teach SwiftUI views and modifiers in Xcode by building a plant header from a Text in the title font and an SF Symbol leaf Image tinted green, with padding around both.

lessons.title: Lay out a card with stacks
lessons.goal: Teach VStack, HStack and Spacer in SwiftUI by arranging the leaf, a plant name and a watering note into a PlantCard view with a rounded background, checked in the Xcode canvas.

lessons.title: A button that changes state

lessons.title: A single neuron
lessons.goal: Teach what one neuron computes using only NumPy in Jupyter. Write neuron(x, w, b) that returns the dot product of inputs and weights plus a bias, and try it on three inputs.

lessons.title: Activation functions
lessons.goal: Teach sigmoid, tanh and ReLU as NumPy functions that work on whole arrays, then add a sigmoid to the neuron so its output stays between 0 and 1.

lessons.title: A layer is a matrix
lessons.goal: Teach a dense layer in NumPy as a weight matrix and a bias vector. Build a layer of 4 neurons that takes 3 inputs and send a batch of 5 samples through it with the @ operator.

lessons.title: The forward pass
lessons.goal: Teach the forward pass of a two-layer network in NumPy. Write forward(X) for a 2-4-1 network that chains a hidden layer with tanh and an output layer with sigmoid.

lessons.title: Measure the error with a loss
lessons.goal: Teach mean squared error and binary cross-entropy in NumPy by writing both as functions and scoring the untrained network's guesses against the right answers.

lessons.title: Gradients by hand

lessons.title: Gradient descent

lessons.title: Backpropagation through two layers

lessons.title: Train a tiny network on XOR
